summary: This case study provides a practical approach for macOS developers and computer-use agents to read Accessibility Zoom viewport coordinates and state directly from the com.apple.universalaccess defaults suite and AX APIs. It addresses a real-world visibility blind spot for applications rendering overlays on magnified displays, offering concrete Swift snippets and geometric transformation formulas. The technical exploration is robust, well-reasoned, and clearly distinguishes between read-only state detection and restricted viewport control mechanisms.
strengths: Addresses a highly specific and practical pain point for macOS developers building overlay UIs and accessibility agents.
Provides clean, usable Swift code snippets for extracting zoom state via both UserDefaults and Accessibility APIs.
Carefully explains coordinate space transformations and clamping logic for secondary and primary displays.
Clearly delineates the limitations of viewport control (preference-gated keyboard shortcuts, cursor warp constraints, and undocumented private APIs).
weaknesses: Relies on undocumented defaults suite keys and notification names that may change across macOS updates.
Picture-in-picture and split-screen geometries rely on approximations rather than fully recovered window chrome decoding.
Linked repository is private, limiting full end-to-end code execution verification.
suggestions: Consider open-sourcing the reference implementation repository to allow direct community testing and verification.
Expand documentation on how distributed notifications handle rapid state changes during active panning.

claims.text: The defaults suite com.apple.universalaccess is readable from an ordinary AppKit process.
CGWarpMouseCursorPosition can be used to recenter fullscreen zoom when zoom follows the cursor continuously.
Option-Command-Arrow pans the zoom window when keyboard shortcuts are enabled in Accessibility system settings.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Screen2AX: Vision-Based Approach for Automatic macOS Accessibility Generation
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While Screen2AX focuses on semantic accessibility metadata for AI agents, this case study targets the specific geometric and viewport boundaries introduced by macOS Accessibility Zoom.
